topic.title: Contextual Bandits and Efficient Decision Policies
topic.overview: Contextual bandits choose actions using features of the current situation while observing only limited outcomes. The topic studies reductions to supervised learning, large or continuous action spaces, warm starts, paid observations, and incentives for exploration. Efficient optimization is as important as a favorable statistical bound.
topic.whyItMatters: Personalized decisions often have too many possible actions for exhaustive scoring. Moreover, users may not accept exploratory recommendations simply because they help the algorithm learn, making incentive compatibility a separate constraint.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives approximate adaptive control with local bandit models. Later methods use optimization oracles and unlabeled contexts to make learning practical. Recent work adds large-action-space optimization, adaptive hyperparameters, and stochastic-context incentive mechanisms. These results depend on different context and reward assumptions and should be compared within matching feedback settings.
openQuestions: How can large-action-space optimization preserve the exploration guarantees of the statistical model?
What is the measurable cost of making exploratory recommendations acceptable to users?
